title: Applied Writing & Creative Compositions (Tasks 5-6)
notes:
Applied Writing & Creative Compositions (Tasks 5 - 6)

Focuses on advanced long-form writing proficiencies spanning professional, personal, and media communication fields.

Composition Modules:

  • Task 5: Applied Correspondence ($1 \times 8 = 8$ Marks): Structuring formal applications, professional CV design, letters to editors, commercial/business letters, and personal communication.
  • Task 6: Extended Composition ($1 \times 10 = 10$ Marks): Creating structured essays, travel memoirs, review frameworks (books/films), biographies, diaries, press releases, and corporate communication updates.
examples:
**Formal Letter to the Editor Layout**

Outline the key structural parts needed in a formal Letter to the Editor.

**Solution:** 1. Sender's Info & Date
2. Recipient Designation (The Editor, Newspaper Name, Address)
3. Clear Subject Line (Underlined/Bold)
4. Formal Salutation
5. Body Paragraphs (Introduction, Cause/Impact, Suggested Solutions)
6. Formal Sign-off (Yours sincerely, Signature, Full Name)
practice: What are the essential layout differences between a formal business letter and a personal letter?
List the core formatting sections that must be present in a professional press release statement.
Draft a complete 250-word model essay structural outline highlighting the Introduction (Hook/Thesis), Body Paragraphs (Topic Sentences/Evidence), and Conclusion (Restatement/Final thought).
keyPoints: Job application letters must include a clean structural layout paired with an organized CV profile.
Review writing should balance objective summaries with critical analysis of themes or performances.
Essays require an obvious progression from initial thesis definitions down to final thematic conclusions.
summary: A practical guide outlining advanced writing topics like personal and corporate letters, custom resume designs, media press releases, essays, and creative memoirs.
